ana: short strawman for unifying hosted/dedicated/private adapter surfaces. posting compact notes so we can flag hard blockers before RFC.

sam: paste please. focusing on auth and cache semantics.

ana: typo, ana :)

ana: heh. ok new post: 1) single minimal handshake at session start: handshake_version, model_id, seq_len_hint, cache_hint, kernel_hint, auth_scheme. 2) runtime Core only consumes hints and returns capability codes; Orchestration owns tenant resolution, auth vending, and routing. 3) provide a bridge binary for legacy adapters to emit the handshake. 4) explicit failure codes (CAPABILITY_MISMATCH, AUTH_REQUIRED) so orch can declaratively fallback.

drew: Core must never see raw tokens. orch should hand a short opaque credref that Core validates via agent-token-proxy over mTLS.

sam: cache_hint enum suggestion: soft_shared, namespace_isolated, pinned. orch maps tenant profile -> hint. Core implements behavior per hint but never receives tenant ids.

lee: ops: require metrics + traces tagged with handshake_version and cache_hint. if CAPABILITY_MISMATCH > 0.5% for 5m, auto-disable handshake flag and route back to legacy.

ana: testing: adapter-faker in CI to simulate orch+bridge+token-proxy. small perf smoke (seq_len distribution) in premerge.

sam: kernel_hint must be advisory; Core returns KERNEL_HINT_IGNORED or KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED so orch can choose alternate paths explicitly.

drew: migration window: canary on dedicated, opt-in hosted, bridge available for private for longer (12mo deprecation notice).

ops-bot: runbook stub: https://internal/ops/runbooks/adapter-handshake.md :white_check_mark:

ana: thanks all 10 will turn into RFC draft with compatibility matrix and test TOC. call out any objections now.

sam: fine from infra side. add PromQL for CAPABILITY_MISMATCH in RFC.

drew: agree. note private installs are slower to upgrade.

ops-bot: reminder: channel retention 90d. archive RFC artifacts in repo.
